mekayis.metin:
(بَزَّ) الْبَاءُ وَالزَّاءُ [أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ] ، وَهُوَ الْهَيْئَةُ مِنْ لِبَاسٍ أَوْ سِلَاحٍ. يُقَالُ: هُوَ بَزَّازٌ يَبِيعُ الْبَزَّ. وَفُلَانٌ حَسَنُ الْبِزَّةِ. وَالْبَزُّ: السِّلَاحُ. قَالَ شَاعِرٌ:
كَأَنِّي إِذْ غَدَوْا ضَمَّنْتُ بَزِّي ... مِنَ الْعِقْبَانِ خَائِتَةً طَلُوبَا
يَقُولُ: كَأَنَّ ثِيَابِي وَسِلَاحِي حِينَ غَدَوْتُ عَلَى عِقَابٍ، مِنْ سُرْعَتِي. وَقَوْلُهُ: خَائِنَةً، تَسْمَعُ لِجَنَاحِهَا صَوْتًا إِذَا انْقَضَّتْ. وَقَوْلُهُمْ بَزَزْتُ الرَّجُلَ، أَيْ: سَلَبْتُهُ، مِنْ هَذَا، لِأَنَّهُ فِعْلٌ وَقَعَ بِبَزِّهِ، كَمَا يُقَالُ: رَأَسْتُهُ: ضَرَبْتُ رَأْسَهُ.
مِمَّا شَذَّ عَنْ هَذَا الْبَابِ الْبَزْبَزَةُ: سُرْعَةُ السَّيْرِ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: بَاز • (bāz) m (plural بِيزَان (bīzān) or أَبْوَاز (ʔabwāz) or بُزَاة (buzāh))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Middle Persian 𐭡𐭠𐭰 (bʾc /⁠bāz⁠/, “hawk, falcon”); cognates with Old Armenian բազէ (bazē), Georgian ბაზი (bazi), Classical Syriac ܒܙܐ (bāzāʾ), and Hebrew בַּז (baz).

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: بَازٍ • (bāzin) m (construct state بَازِي (bāzī), plural بَوَازٍ (bawāzin, construct state بَوَازِي (bawāzī)) or بُزَاة (buzāh) or بِيزَان (bīzān))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Middle Persian 𐭡𐭠𐭰 (bʾc /⁠bāz⁠/, “hawk, falcon”); cognates with Old Armenian բազէ (bazē), Georgian ბაზი (bazi), Classical Syriac ܒܙܐ (bāzāʾ), and Hebrew בַּז (baz).

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: بِزّ or بُزّ • (bizz or buzz) m (plural بِزَاز (bizāz) or أَبْزَاز (ʔabzāz))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Cognate to Aramaic בִּיזָא, ܒܷܙܐ (bizzā, “teat”), בּוּזָא (buzzā, “teat”), Ugaritic 𐎁𐎑 (bẓ, “teat”). Differently Akkadian 𒍣𒍣𒂊 (/⁠zīzu⁠/, “teat”), Hebrew זִיז (zīz, “abundance, teat, protuberance”), Hebrew דַּד (dad, “teat”), Aramaic דַּדָּא (daddā, “teat”).

Ultimately a re-borrowing from what was originally a Semitic source (Akkadian 𒁍𒌋𒋗 (bu-u-ṣu /⁠būṣu⁠/)); see also بِزَّة (bizza, “suit”).
* Borrowed from Old Armenian բեհեզ (behez) or the earlier Old Armenian *բեեզ (*beez)
* Alternatively, a clipping of بُزْيُون (buzyūn, “a kind of silk garment”), from Medieval Greek βυσσίνη (bussínē), or from Ancient Greek βύσσος (bússos, “a very fine yellowish flax and the linen woven from it”).
s: Ancient Greek βύσσος (bússos, “a very fine yellowish flax and the linen woven from it”)

g: to strip off, to spoil, to remove by force

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Classical Persian پوز (pōz, “the lip, mouth, and environs; the beak of a bird, the snout of a quadruped; the space between the nose and lip; the trunk of a tree”), akin to Northern Kurdish pîj (“splinter”).
s: Classical Persian پوز (pōz, “the lip, mouth, and environs; the beak of a bird, the snout of a quadruped; the space between the nose and lip; the trunk of a tree”)
g: a wooden pin protruding from a door (traditional in Tetouan) by which it attaches in place of hinges

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: بَوَّزَ • (bawwaza) II (non-past يُبَوِّزُ (yubawwizu), verbal noun تَبْوِيز (tabwīz))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Classical Persian پوز (pōz, “the lip, mouth, and environs; the beak of a bird, the snout of a quadruped; the space between the nose and lip; the trunk of a tree”), akin to Northern Kurdish pîj (“splinter”).
s: Classical Persian پوز (pōz, “the lip, mouth, and environs; the beak of a bird, the snout of a quadruped; the space between the nose and lip; the trunk of a tree”)
g: to pout, to grimace with the mouth
alternative form of بُوظة (būẓa, “(Levantine) ice cream”)

kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From English buzz, possibly with allusion to the door-pin sense above.
